rules.label: ETA or eVisitor: up to 3 months per visit
notes: The ETA (subclass 601) and eVisitor (subclass 651) let you visit as often as you like while they're valid (usually 12 months), staying up to 3 months each time.
A Visitor visa (subclass 600) can allow 3, 6 or 12 months. If you have one, check the stay period on your grant notice.
New Zealand citizens get a Special Category visa on arrival and can stay indefinitely.

rules.label: 183-day test: 183 days in the income year
notes: The Australian income year runs from 1 July to 30 June. Days don't need to be in a row, and the days you arrive and leave count.
183 days usually makes you resident, but not if your usual home is outside Australia and you don't intend to live there.
You can be resident with fewer days under the 'resides' or domicile tests, for example if you've moved to Australia.
